rules: Each scenario is created and run on both products with the same name, instructions and trigger semantics.
Instructions are copied verbatim; only product-specific trigger wiring differs.
A scenario passes only if: creation succeeds, the trigger starts a run without manual help, the run finishes, and the outcome check below holds.
Timings: create = first click on Create to saved automation; start latency = trigger event to run/session start; run = start to finish (from each product's own run record).
Every PR an automation opens is checked by CI on GitHub (the fixture's CI runs npm test).

scenarios.name: bench-A1 scheduled changelog

trigger.detail: a run a few minutes after creation (Devin: Run once / Custom; NeoDevEx: cron)

scenarios.instructions: In vamsi920/automation-bench, add the line "- Benchmark run A1." under the "## 1.0.0" heading in CHANGELOG.md, then open a pull request titled "bench A1: changelog". Change nothing else.
scenarios.check: A PR titled 'bench A1: changelog' exists whose diff only adds that line to CHANGELOG.md.

scenarios.name: bench-A2 fix discount bug

trigger.detail: Run now / dispatch on an automation with a far-future schedule

scenarios.instructions: In vamsi920/automation-bench, fix GitHub issue #1 (10% discount gives a negative total). Run npm test until it passes for the discount test, then open a pull request titled "bench A2: fix discount" that references #1. Do not change the tests.
scenarios.check: PR exists, does not modify test/, and its CI run of the discount test passes.

scenarios.name: bench-A3 webhook issue fix

trigger.detail: HTTP POST with JSON {"issue": 2} to the automation's webhook URL

scenarios.instructions: A webhook delivered a JSON payload naming an issue number in vamsi920/automation-bench. Read that issue, fix it, run npm test, and open a pull request titled "bench A3: fix issue <number>" that references it. Do not change the tests.
scenarios.check: PR titled 'bench A3: fix issue 2' exists and changes shippingCents to free shipping at >= 5000.

scenarios.name: bench-A4 /bench comment

trigger.detail: comment starting with /bench on any issue in the repo

scenarios.instructions: Someone commented /bench on an issue in vamsi920/automation-bench. Reply on that issue with a one-paragraph plan for fixing it, then stop.
scenarios.check: A reply comment appears on the issue that received the /bench comment.

scenarios.name: bench-A5 fix failing CI

trigger.detail: a failed CI check run on a pull request

scenarios.instructions: A CI check failed on a pull request in vamsi920/automation-bench. Read the failing job's log, push a fix to that pull request's branch so CI passes, and comment on the PR with what you changed.
scenarios.check: A fix commit lands on the failing PR's branch and CI turns green.

scenarios.name: bench-A6 template: weekly changelog

trigger.detail: each product's built-in changelog/release-notes template, then run it once manually

scenarios.check: Template creates without edits beyond choosing the repo, runs, and produces a changelog PR or report.

scenarios.name: bench-A7 create from a sentence

trigger.detail: Devin: Generate with Devin. NeoDevEx: create from chat.

scenarios.instructions: Every weekday at 9am, check vamsi920/automation-bench for open issues with no comments and post a short triage note on each.
scenarios.check: An automation exists afterwards with a weekday 9am schedule, the right repo, and instructions matching the sentence.

scenarios.name: bench-A8 failure surfacing

trigger.detail: run an automation pointed at a repository that does not exist: vamsi920/automation-bench-missing

scenarios.instructions: In vamsi920/automation-bench-missing, add a README line and open a PR.
scenarios.check: The run fails visibly with a clear reason in the product's run view; no silent success and no stuck 'running' state.

scenarios.name: bench-A9 review new PRs

trigger.detail: a pull request is opened in the fixture repo

scenarios.instructions: A pull request was opened in vamsi920/automation-bench. Review its diff for bugs, missing tests and anything that would break CI, and post one review comment on the PR with concrete findings (file and line) and a verdict: approve, or request changes.
scenarios.check: Exactly one review comment on the new PR, naming the planted bug's file and line, with a verdict.

scenarios.name: bench-A10 triage new issues

trigger.detail: an issue is opened in the fixture repo

scenarios.instructions: An issue was opened in vamsi920/automation-bench. Read it and the relevant code, then post one triage comment: type (bug/feature/question), priority P0-P3, the likely file and function, and a suggested next step.
scenarios.check: Exactly one triage comment on the new issue that names the right file and function.
